title: Constraint: Five Bits, Sometimes Consecutive
constraints: In about **30 %** of results the five ones are **contiguous** (e.g. `0000_0011_1110_0000`), otherwise they are not.
Runs on Verilator with the z3 solver (`sudo pacman -S z3`).
hints: Five ones are contiguous exactly when `v & (v >> 1)` has **four** ones. Verilator's constraint-to-SMT translation mis-sizes shift operators on vectors narrower than 32 bits (z3 then rejects the query and `randomize()` fails). Use part-selects and concatenation instead: `v >> 1` becomes `{1'b0, v[15:1]}`.
Helper bit: `rand bit run; run dist {1 := 30, 0 := 70};` and `run == ($countones(v & (v >> 1)) == 4);`.
Without the helper, contiguous patterns (12 of 4368) would almost never appear.

examples.check: the 5 ones are consecutive in about 30 %
